summary.headline: Ashoka Buildcon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA fell 55% YoY to INR292 crores on HAM/BOT monetisation; FY27 revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20%.
summary.overview: Standalone total income was flat YoY at INR1,320 crores, with EBITDA down 17% to INR126 crores (9.5% margin) and PAT up 3% to INR31.5 crores. Consolidated total income fell 21% to INR1,534 crores, mainly because of BOT and HAM asset monetisation in Q3 FY26, and consolidated EBITDA fell 55% to INR292 crores (19.0% margin). Management cut FY27 revenue growth guidance to 10-15% from 20% and EBITDA margin to roughly 9-9.5% from about 10%. Order book stood at INR15,251 crores as of 30 June, with about INR450 crores added after quarter-end, and the company is pivoting to international, railway and power T&D work as domestic highway awarding stays subdued.

segments.commentary: Contributed 49.3% of standalone revenue in Q1 FY27. Order book about INR6,780 crores.

segments.commentary: Contributed 10.2% of standalone revenue. About INR1,500 crores of HAM order book; six HAM projects had about INR638 crores invested to June.

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: Contributed 18.4% of standalone revenue. Order book about INR5,066 crores (33.2%), but collections slowed and are expected to normalise by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Railway
segments.commentary: Contributed 11.5% of standalone revenue. Order book about INR1,346 crores.

segments.name: Building EPC and others
segments.commentary: Contributed 10.7% of standalone revenue. Building EPC order book INR536 crores (3.5%).

segments.name: BOT (Jaora-Nayagaon)
segments.commentary: Gross toll collection of INR75 crores in Q1, up 8% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth lowered to 10-15% from 20% earlier, citing a flat Q1 and supply-chain uncertainty.
FY27 EBITDA margin about 0.5 percentage points below the start-of-year target of roughly 10%, i.e. around 9-9.5%; margin recovery expected in H2 as new projects ramp up.
FY27 order inflow guided at INR6,000-8,000 crores: INR800 crores won in Q1, plus about INR1,800 crores where the company is L1 (expected to materialise in Q2), with the rest in Q3-Q4.

Asset monetisation of about INR1,150 crores (quoted as INR1,100 crores later in the call): four assets targeted by September 2026 (about INR700 crores) and two assets by Q4 FY27. Chennai ORR expected by year-end; Jaora-Nayagaon by March 2027 or H1 FY28.
Post-monetisation third-party debt guided at INR500-600 crores; total debt including subsidiary debt about INR1,100-1,200 crores.

FY28 margins expected to improve to 10.5-11% on projects, per management; standalone interest cost guided to about INR200-210 crores for FY28, versus INR225-240 crores for FY26 (INR313 crores was cited for FY26 by an analyst; the management figure for FY25 was INR225-240 crores).
HAM equity requirement: INR179 crores for FY27 on existing HAM projects (including Bowaichandi), then INR72 crores each in FY28 and FY29.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex about INR25 crores (INR7 crores international); FY27 capex target about INR125 crores.
Bowaichandi HAM appointed date expected first week of October 2026; about 15% of work expected this fiscal year.
Mithi River project has started; Guyana work is ongoing; Angola expected to start in about two months.

Guyana four-laning (Versailles-Parika) order valued at USD35.42 million, about INR328-338 crores (figures differ in the transcript); Gems and Jewellery Park PPP (JV, 51% stake) about INR450 crores, with a possible investment of about INR1,000 crores over five years, recovered over the same period.
Purestudy stake diluted from 59% to 39.33%, making it an associate rather than a subsidiary.
demand_pricing: NHAI awarded about 5 km of projects in June 2026 versus 102 km in May; construction in June fell 32% YoY to about 274 km; April-May construction about 638 km, down 34% YoY.
Bid pipeline: NHAI/MoRTH about INR1 lakh crore, states about INR25,000 crore, railways about INR50,000 crore; bids submitted but not yet opened about INR8,000 crore.
Order book INR15,251 crores as of 30 June (excluding about INR450 crores won after quarter-end). Road and railway about 63.3% (INR9,648 crores), Power T&D about 33.2%, building EPC about 3.5%.
International presence in 7 countries, with a plan to reach about 10. Margins and competition vary by country.
Management expects good road awarding in Q3-Q4 FY27 and says NHAI is moving to larger packages, which should rationalise competition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current bid pipeline, by sector, and how much is bid but not yet opened?
qa_highlights.answer: NHAI/MoRTH about INR1 lakh crore, states about INR25,000 crore, railways about INR50,000 crore, plus power T&D and renewables EPC bids. Bids submitted but not yet opened total about INR8,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth guidance changed and what is the order inflow and margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth guidance cut to 10-15% from 20% because Q1 was flat amid supply-chain and other uncertainty. Order inflow guided at INR6,000-8,000 crore: INR800 crore won in Q1, L1 in about INR1,800 crore expected to convert in Q2. FY27 margin about 0.5 pp below the roughly 10% start-of-year target, with H2 ramp-up expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline and realisation for the asset monetisation, and are there holdbacks?
qa_highlights.answer: Four assets targeted by September-end or early October for about INR700 crore; remaining two by Q4 FY27. Total about INR1,100-1,150 crore (management called it a rounding). Holdbacks of about INR30-40 crore possible; about 30% of previously monetised amounts received so far.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and interest cost outlook after monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Third-party debt post-monetisation about INR500-600 crore; total including subsidiary debt about INR1,100-1,200 crore. Subsidiary interest in Q1 was INR17 crore. Standalone interest cost about INR60 crore in Q1, expected near INR50 crore by year-end; FY28 interest guided at INR200-210 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall in Q1 and will FY28 margins recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 costs were loaded by new administrative staff and overheads for new verticals, expected to rationalise over coming quarters. FY28 projects are expected to deliver margins of about 10.5-11%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Chennai ORR and Jaora-Nayagaon monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai ORR expected by year-end, pending investor freeze; Jaora-Nayagaon by March-end 2027 or H1 FY28, dependent on authority compliance. Equity invested: Jaora total project equity INR278 crore, company's acquired-stake cost about INR418 crore; Chennai ORR effective cost about INR300 crore for 100%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the economics of the Gems and Jewellery Park and Guyana orders, and how is overseas revenue split?
qa_highlights.answer: Gems and Jewellery Park (51% JV, INR450 crore contract) could yield about INR100 crore a year over five years; overall project size about INR1,000 crore over five years. Guyana four-laning valued at about INR338 crore. Q1 overseas revenue about INR145 crore, about 80% from Guyana.

risks_watch: Domestic highway awarding remains subdued: only about 5 km awarded in June and construction down 32% YoY in June, so Q3-Q4 awarding recovery is a key test.
Margin guidance cut to roughly 9-9.5%: H2 ramp-up depends on new projects scaling and on cost rationalisation of new verticals.

Monetisation timing and holdbacks: four assets targeted by September, two by Q4 FY27, with possible holdbacks of INR30-40 crore and about INR140-150 crore of earlier deal amounts still being received.
Power T&D collections slowed, with management expecting normalisation only by Q4 FY27; working capital rose by about INR250 crore from March to June.
Order inflow of INR6,000-8,000 crore for FY27 depends on converting about INR1,800 crore L1 positions in Q2 and on the Q3-Q4 awards.
Overseas concentration: about 80% of Q1 overseas revenue came from Guyana; the company plans to expand to about 10 countries.
key_quotes: So guidance, we are lowering down from 20% to between 10% to 15% because this quarter has been flat due to various reasons and various uncertainties, particularly supply chain.
H1 will continue to remain subdued, but H2 will definitely ramp up and there we'll catch up with 9.5% of EBITDA based on whatever we are spending for the new projects which are taking off.
So these debt need not be reduced because they are typically free cash flows of our subsidiaries.
So Q3, Q4, we expect good awarding to happen.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on diversification into international, railway and power T&D wins and on the long-term road outlook. It was cautious and at times evasive on near-term domestic awarding, margin recovery timing, and monetisation holdbacks, and deferred several granular numbers (SPV order book, FY27 revenue from specific projects) to offline follow-up.
